subject: Next steps: deployment venue confirmation & legacy API exit ladder
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thornton <claire@novamed.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + ask after today's demo

Hi Claire — thanks for taking the demo with us this morning. Quick recap and the few asks we promised: 

What we heard from you:
- Primary requirement: sub-50ms p95 inference for short clinical prompts (avg 40 tokens) for the triage assistant.
- Data residency: patient meta must remain in your VPC; PII cannot be logged to a third-party control plane.
- Migration source: you are currently on a self-hosted cluster (legacy GPU autoscaler) with an internal API fronting models (we saw usage ~150k tokens/day).
- Procurement window: aiming to finalize vendor and deployment by end of Q2.

Options we recommended on call (brief):
1) Hosted API (fastest time-to-value) — we can mask PII and minimize logs, but it requires our hosted control plane (not ideal for strict residency).
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool in our infra; data streaming goes to your endpoints but control plane remains with Redwood; good balance for throughput/SLA.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — full customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem runtime; matches your residency requirement but longer lead time.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether Novamed will accept a Dedicated deployment with an encrypted traffic proxy (we'd keep only aggregated telemetry)?
2) If not, can we get a short list of procurement and security approvers so we can start the VPC onboarding checklist?
3) Are there any existing custom tokenizers or model forks in your cluster we need to import?

Attaching: Redwood_SLA_Standard_2028.pdf and a migration-checklist-template.xlsx for you to share with procurement/security.

Next step suggestion: a 60-minute technical deep dive next week with your infra + security and our infra/RE team to walk the VPC onramp or Dedicated configuration (whichever you prefer).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
---
On Tue, Mar 30, 2028 at 08:05 AM Claire Thornton <claire@novamed.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo — highlights were the latency profile and the KV cache examples.
>
> A few clarifications from our side:
> - We cannot send any PHI to an external control plane, even if encrypted. That rules out Hosted API unless we can guarantee zero PII leaves our VPC (difficult for Hosted).
> - Our legacy cluster exposes a model-compatibility layer (internal API) that your runtime would need to accept during cutover.
> - Procurement wants estimated monthly committed spend for Dedicated (GPU count + reserved throughput).
>
> Will loop in procurement next.
> —Claire

From: Claire Thornton <claire@novamed.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.ai>
Date: 2028-03-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask after today's demo

Jordan — thanks for the writeup and attachments. A quick reply from procurement/security: 

Procurement asks:
- Rough committed monthly cost for a Dedicated 4xA100 pool serving the triage workload (150k tokens/day, burst 4x). Please include a POC pricing band.

Security asks:
- For Dedicated: can audit logs and request payloads be delivered to our SIEM (we use Splunk Cloud) and retained only inside our account?
- For Private VPC: estimated timeline (weeks) to have a VPC control plane + runtime deployed on our Azure tenant.

Also flagging one blocker: our internal model registry uses a slightly different tokenizer mapping; if we go with Private VPC, we'll want to ship the tokenizer config and weights.

Claire

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thornton <claire@novamed.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-31T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask after today's demo

Claire — great questions. Short answers, then proposed plan.

Answers:
- Dedicated pricing: rough committed band for a 4xA100 pool (reserved) + 99.9% SLA is in the attached POC worksheet; ballpark: $44k–$60k/month depending on commit length and burst allowance. I'll ask Priyom to get a formal quote and term options.
- Audit logs to Splunk: yes — for Dedicated we can ship structured audit logs (no PII) to your Splunk ingestion endpoint; for Private we can export full request/response logs directly to your storage account under your control.
- VPC timeline (Azure): typical VPC control plane + runtime in your tenant is 4–6 weeks after contract signature (includes KMS/HSM integration and penetration test window).
- Tokenizer migration: we have an import path for custom tokenizers in the Private flow. For Dedicated we can mount a tokenizer bundle during rollout; we recommend doing tokenizer parity validation in a POC.

Proposed migration approach (minimizes risk):
1) POC (2 weeks): Stand up a Dedicated sandbox with a single model replica, replicate a subset of your traffic (non-PHI) via proxy, validate latency and tokenizer parity.
2) Parallel run (4 weeks): Ramp routing 10%/30%/60%/100% from legacy cluster to Redwood Dedicated. Monitor quality/regressions via the eval set you provided.
3) Cutover: If all gates pass, either keep Dedicated long-term or convert to Private VPC for full data residency and control-plane handoff.

Attachments: POC quote request submitted (see migration-checklist-template.xlsx) and the SLA.

Next steps I propose: 
- Prio 1: Priyom to deliver a formal Dedicated quote and POC pricing by EOD Thursday.
- Prio 2: Schedule the technical deep dive (infra + security). Can your team do next Wednesday 10:00am PT?

If you want, we can also prepare a short runbook for the 10%/30% ramp with rollback conditions.

—Jordan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thornton <claire@novamed.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-31T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated quote + POC band for Novamed (follow-up)

Hi Claire — looping in a few numbers as requested. These are POC-band estimates; final pricing depends on contract term and exact burst policy.

Estimated POC band (Dedicated 4xA100 reserved pool):
- Monthly reserved fee (baseline throughput): $36,000/month (1-year commit)
- Burst buffer (cost allocated to usage above baseline): metered; expected +$6k–$12k/month depending on burst profile.
- POC one-time setup: $8,500 (includes tokenizer parity run and Splunk connector setup)

Notes:
- SLA: 99.9% for Dedicated; option to add premium SLA for additional fee.
- For Private VPC, we will provide a separate SOW — typically an uplift of ~25–40% on committed fees to account for control plane transfer, KMS integration, and on-prem runtime packaging.

Action items I need from Novamed to finalize:
1) Confirmation if PII/PHI can be redacted for the POC traffic (recommended) or if all traffic must remain in your tenant (then we move to VPC POC).
2) Splunk ingestion endpoint for log forwarding (if Dedicated).
3) Contact for procurement to start a standard MSA review (procurement@novamed.ai noted).

I'll follow up with a formal quote PDF by Thursday EOD.

Thanks — Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Thornton <claire@novamed.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.ai>
Date: 2028-04-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated quote + POC band for Novamed (follow-up)

Thanks team — this is helpful. Procurement confirmed they can provision a sandbox Splunk ingestion endpoint for the POC and will share the contact later today. Security confirmed we prefer a Private VPC in the long term, but ok to run the POC on Dedicated if you can guarantee that no PHI leaves our tenant during the POC (we will redact PHI for initial traffic).

Accepted next steps:
- Novamed to redact PHI for POC traffic (we will handle).
- Priyom to send formal POC quote PDF + sample SOW for Private VPC uplift.
- Schedule the technical deep dive on 2028-04-04 10:00am PT — Claire, I'll invite our infra and security leads.

Looking forward — Claire
Head of ML Platform, Novamed
